intended_object: The diagonal embedding of the rank-N split torus into GL_N on A-points, for a commutative R-algebra A: (t₁,…,t_N) ↦ diag(t₁,…,t_N). Points are taken as R-algebra maps out of the coordinate Hopf algebras with convolution product. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation (Milne §21).
explanation:
The definition is a chain of four maps. First, the split-torus points equivalence identifies algebra maps out of R[ℤ^{ULift (Fin N)}] with families ULift (Fin N) → Aˣ. Second, `diagonalTorusCoordinates` restricts such a family to Fin N; the ULift is only there for universe bookkeeping. Third, `diagGL` sends a family of units to the invertible diagonal matrix built from them (Units.map of Matrix.diagonalRingHom). Fourth, the inverse of the GL points equivalence turns that matrix back into an algebra map out of the coordinate Hopf algebra of GL_N.

The result is exactly the diagonal embedding T(A) → GL_N(A) at the level of points, and it is a group homomorphism. The library proves the expected facts about it: it is injective, it is natural in A, and conjugating by it acts on root subgroups by the characters t ↦ t_i t_j⁻¹. It is also used to build the group-scheme morphism.

Mathlib has neither the GL_N group scheme nor its diagonal torus, so there is nothing more general to compare it with. Indexing by Fin N is not too narrow: the object is the specific standard torus of GL_N, and the library's GL_N coordinate Hopf algebra is itself indexed by N.
